newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Fuel shortage seen forcing Chernobyl shutdown April.
newsitem.headline: Fuel shortage seen forcing Chernobyl shutdown April.

text.p: Ukraine's Chernobyl nuclear power plant, owed millions of dollars by consumers, has halved its output and a fuel shortage could force it to shut down its sole working reactor in a month, a spokesman said on Thursday.

"Late last night the working capacity of the third reactor was reduced by 50 percent. The station lacks fuel. We can operate for one month with what we have left," the plant's chief spokesman, Valery Idelson, told Reuters. "If there is no fuel we will stop the reactor," he added.
Idelson said consumers owed Chernobyl more than 200 million hryvnias ($110 million) and the station had no money to buy more fuel from Russia.
The plant has been operating on fuel obtained in return for Ukraine giving up nuclear warheads to Russia under a 1994 deal signed by Kiev, Moscow and Washington.
Western countries have pledged $3.1 billion in credits and aid to enable Ukraine to meet President Leonid Kuchma's promise to close the station by year 2000.

Eleven years ago next month reactor No. 4 caught fire and exploded, sending clouds of radiation across Europe. The second reactor was stopped in 1991 after a small fire while the first one closed last November in line with the programme.
